notes: 2026-10月定期更新。exoplanet.eu 2026-10-06 を統合: 追記132行のうち重複81件を引き継ぎ統合、新規50惑星、6587惑星×158列。★公開中のカタログに同一惑星の二重登録(TIC 46432937 b = TOI-7716 b)が前から入っていたのを統合(周期・質量・半径・座標が小数13桁まで一致、消える側にしか無かった31列のキュレーション済みデータを引き継いだ)。別名の誤り3件を修正。★SIMBADで全4,935ホストを照会し3,969ホストの座標を確定。123件の大きな誤りを修正(赤緯の符号反転5件=バルジ天体が北天になっていた、Kepler視野の座標混入8件=NASAで裏付け、桁の取り違え多数)。六十分法7列・視差・SIMBAD識別子を新規充填(入っていること自体が検証済みの印になる)。ADSで文献を410行補完(Title/Abstract 80.2%→86.5%)。★ADSの検索式が全滅していたのを修正し、1882年のNatureを発見論文として掴む誤りを門で止めた。NASA ps 2026-10-06版でトランジット3,816セル充填。★GJ 4274のE_maxを1.18e35から2.509e33へ降格(FFD外挿が観測最大の47倍、CROWDSAP 0.4529で混入源を切り分けられない。TESSAll 2026-10-07再計算)。★ハビタブル候補ホスト10個の恒星パラメータを実測値で確定(分光型が取れない星にM型の既定値3300K/0.400R☉を当てていた。HD 48948は実際にはK3V 4593Kで光度が一桁違っていた)。光度を正とし、R*はそれと整合する値を書いた。結果ハビタブルは79→77個(GJ 4274 b / HD 48948 c / K2-296 b が外れ、HD 48948 d が入った)。補完値に依存する判定はゼロになった。

paleo_planets.purpose: Stage-labeled paleo Solar System (ASol d/e/c stage variants, Custom1..4 metadata). Codex 2026-05-30.

AsolInfo.purpose: Numeric-epoch paleo Solar System (ASol b/c/d/e/f/g/h/i × 500/1000/2000/3000/4000 MY). Per-epoch evolving star activity (Aspot_u, Prot, star_age, star_teff). User-authored 2026-06-02.

Binary_Master.purpose: Binary star system master (separation_au, period_days, planet_orbit_type, physical_info, member_aliases). Source: gaia/binary/Binary_Master.xlsx.

alfven.format: CSV (11 cols: host_name, planet_name, B_gauss, Prot_d, Prot_conf, r_A_au, a_over_rA, regime, Hu_bin, method, source)
alfven.purpose: Alfven-surface classification per planet: stellar magnetic field from rotation, Alfven radius (split-monopole, v_w=400 km/s), a/r_A, and sub/borderline/super-Alfvenic regime with Hu bin. Source: TESSAll recompute 2026-08-31 (160 planets / 82 hosts) plus 2026-09-01 addendum (GJ 1002 b/c, Kepler-1638 b). Covers all 79 habitable-zone planets. Kept out of the 158-column master by design: the column count is a hard constraint and the C++ reader holds fixed column offsets. Values are NOT duplicated into revision_note, because numbers buried in prose stop being machine-readable and break per-row provenance.
alfven.unbound_note: These planets are not present in the 158-column master. Reported rather than dropped, so the discrepancy stays visible.

flare_ffd.format: CSV (11 cols: host_name, host_name_tessall, FFD_alpha, FFD_beta, n_flares_real, n_flares_candidate, obs_time_days, E_max_1yr_erg, E_max_method, alpha_reliable, source)
flare_ffd.purpose: Flare frequency distribution per host: power-law index FFD_alpha, normalisation FFD_beta, real/candidate flare counts, observing baseline, and the reliability flag. E_max alone is the single largest flare expected in a year; alpha governs the CUMULATIVE dose, which can differ by orders of magnitude at the same E_max. Source: TESSAll recompute 2026-08-31, extracted 2026-09-01 without new analysis. alpha present for 7 of 81 hosts, reliable for 5 (GJ 3323, GJ 4274, Gl 725 B, Kepler-1646, Proxima Centauri). Unreliable values are carried, not dropped: 'not trustworthy' is different information from 'absent'.
flare_ffd.host_name_note: host_name is the ExoKyoto star_name; host_name_tessall preserves the TESSAll spelling. 12 hosts were remapped through an explicit table, never by prefix matching -- 'Kepler-78' also prefixes 'Kepler-780 A', and guessing a name silently ships another star's numbers.
flare_ffd.correction_note: GJ 4274 corrected 2026-10-07: the FFD-1yr extrapolation of 1.180230e35 erg was withdrawn (it is ~47x the observed maximum, and CROWDSAP median 0.4529 means TESS photometry cannot separate the flare source from a nearby one). Now carries the observed maximum, 2.509003e33 erg. ★alpha=-0.6429 itself is unchanged and still marked reliable; what was withdrawn is the extrapolated energy, not the slope.

xuv_shoreline.format: CSV (19 cols: planet_name, host_name, alpha_used, alpha_source, xuv_cumulative_erg_cm2, integration_gyr, escape_metric, shoreline_side, shoreline_margin, method, source, age_gyr_used, age_source, mass_me_used, mass_source, vesc_kms, xuv_rel_earth, flare_frac, host_name_tessall)
xuv_shoreline.purpose: Cosmic shoreline for all 79 habitable-zone planets: lifetime-integrated XUV (saturated phase then t^-1.5 decay, plus the flare contribution from the FFD) against the Zahnle & Catling (2017) v_esc^4 criterion. retain 25 / boundary 36 / escape 18. Sanity check on the Solar System: Earth sits ON the boundary (margin -0.00) and Mars escapes (-1.02), so the normalisation is self-consistent. shoreline_side is three-valued and shoreline_margin (dex) is carried alongside, because the boundary itself is uncertain and a two-valued answer would hide that.
xuv_shoreline.assumptions_note: Assumptions are columns, not hidden constants. alpha_source: measured 4, literature default 72, NO_DATA 3. age_source: measured 46, ASSUMED 5.0 Gyr 31, solar canonical 2. mass_source records whether the mass is measured, m sin i, or inferred from radius.
xuv_shoreline.null_result_note: Recomputed 2026-09-03 after the Sun was given a literature E_max (Carrington-class, 5e32 erg) and after the Kepler-1649 E_max correction of four orders of magnitude. ★NOTHING MOVED: all 79 margins are identical to four decimals and no planet changed class (retain 25 / boundary 36 / escape 18). The reason is quantitative, not a coincidence - the flare contribution to the integrated XUV is about 1e-6 of the quiescent term (flare_frac 0.00), so even treating a once-per-century Carrington event as annual does not reach the decision. Two independent tests now say the same thing: a 1e4 change at Kepler-1649 and a literature value at the Sun. Atmospheric loss here is set by saturated-phase quiescent XUV, not by flares. Earth stays ON the boundary by construction - it is the normalisation anchor, and the same flare term was added to the denominator to keep that self-consistent - but Mars staying outside (-1.02) is not by construction.

gyro_ages.format: CSV (11 cols: host_name, host_name_tessall, Prot_d, Prot_confidence, teff_used, bv_used, gyro_age_gyr, gyro_valid, note, method, source)
gyro_ages.purpose: Gyrochronology ages per host from the rotation period (Mamajek & Hillenbrand 2008; B-V from Teff via Pecaut & Mamajek 2013). 81 hosts; an age is produced for 81 and gyro_valid is True for 47. Activity declines with age, so without an age one cannot tell whether an observed high flare rate is what the star IS or merely how young it is. gyro_valid=False marks fully convective stars (Teff<3300 K) outside the calibration: the value is carried with a note, because 'outside calibration' is different information from 'absent'. Hosts with LOW/NONE rotation confidence are NO_DATA rather than guessed.

flare_clustering.format: CSV (11 cols: host_name, host_name_tessall, n_flares_real, obs_span_d, waiting_cv, clustering, max_E_frac_30d, top10pct_time_flare_frac, method, source, status)
flare_clustering.purpose: Temporal clustering of flares for the 6 hosts with at least 10 real flares. E_max says how big, alpha says how often, but neither says whether the energy arrives in bursts or evenly - and the atmospheric response differs. waiting_cv is the coefficient of variation of inter-flare waiting times (Poisson gives ~1; larger means clustered), with the largest 30-day energy fraction and the flare fraction falling in the densest 10% of the baseline. Restricted to 6 hosts on purpose: below ~10 flares the statistic is meaningless, and reporting that it cannot be measured is worth more than filling all 79.

solar_alfven_evolution.format: CSV (8 cols: age_Gyr, rA_may_AU, rA_sep_AU, ratio_may_over_sep, regime_Earth_may, B_may_G, Mdot_may, vw_may)
solar_alfven_evolution.purpose: Evolution of the Solar Alfven radius, 0.07 to 4.57 Gyr, on the canonical (JpGU, 2026-05) track: the young Sun's large-scale field is anchored to the EK Dra ZDI measurement of ~100 G (Folsom et al. 2018), so the decay of B dominates and r_A SHRINKS with age - 1.598 AU at 0.07 Gyr, 0.902 AU at 0.2 Gyr, 0.046 AU today. ★Earth was therefore sub-Alfvenic - inside the solar magnetosphere - for roughly its first 200 Myr, crossed through borderline near 0.2 Gyr, and has been super-Alfvenic ever since, while keeping its atmosphere (it sits ON the cosmic shoreline, margin -0.00; Mars does not, -1.02). So super-Alfvenic does not mean atmospheric loss, and the 9 retain-AND-super planets in the habitable-zone sample are not a contradiction. The column rA_sep_AU carries the SUPERSEDED 2026-09 reconstruction for comparison only: it applied the relative stellar-comparison scaling to a single star's absolute history, which inverted the sign of the trend. Both tracks agree exactly at 4.57 Gyr (0.046 AU), and that agreement is the cross-check.
solar_alfven_evolution.correction_note: Supersedes the version published 2026-09-02, whose purpose text stated that Earth is super-Alfvenic at every epoch. That was wrong: it rested on the 2026-09 reconstruction, now identified as an artifact. Absolute values before ~1 Gyr depend on a single B(t) anchor (EK Dra), which is stated rather than hidden.
